title: SG-4.2.3 · Enforce the tracked-dependency check in the test script
summary: Wire a tracked-dependency guard into npm test so it fails when any node_modules or vitest-cache path is tracked by git.
description: Context: game/frontend/src/lib/trackedNodeModules.ts has trackedNodeModulesPaths, untrackNodeModules and assertNoTrackedNodeModules, but nothing runs them and package.json test is plain `vitest run`. Desired behavior: a null-separated git ls-files check (checkTrackedFiles, parseGitLsFiles), a guard CLI script, and a test script that runs the guard before vitest. Expected result: npm test fails if a dependency or test-cache path is tracked. Why: stops vendored Phaser files from being committed again.
acceptance_criteria: Given git ls-files -z output containing a node_modules or .vite/vitest path, When checkTrackedFiles runs, Then it reports that path.
Given a tracked dependency path, When the guard CLI logic runs, Then it prints the paths and returns a non-zero exit code.
Given package.json, When the test script is read, Then it runs the guard before vitest run.
Given tsc --noEmit, When run, Then tests/trackedNodeModules.test.ts and the new guard tests produce no type errors.

in_scope: unit tests with a fake git runner
preserve: Existing trackedNodeModulesPaths, untrackNodeModules, assertNoTrackedNodeModules behavior and exports

technical_constraints: vite-node runs the guard script (already used by untrack:node-modules)
No duplicate exports in the helper file
Unit tests use a fake git runner, never real git
definition_of_done: All three requirements have passing unit tests
npm test script includes the guard
